investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for ~141–145 seconds, exceeding the eval's timeout, and no required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever produced.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 are eligible by node affinity/selector for remote agent pods, and both of those nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. Preemption was also ruled out (no preemption victims found). Because the pod could not be scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885) never returned a VM identity or state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion localized to the remote-agent scheduling tier; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing running remote agent VMs or leaked/zombie pods that were not cleaned up, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling.
[Likely] A recent surge in remote agent creation requests exhausted the fixed pool of peer-pod VM slots before the eval ran, and the cluster has not yet reclaimed capacity.

[Possible] One or both of the 2 affinity-eligible nodes became degraded, cordoned, or had their kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable count reduced (e.g., node maintenance, resource reconfiguration), shrinking available capacity without a corresponding scale-out.

[Possible] The 4 nodes that did not match node affinity/selector were recently added or relabeled and lack the required node labels or taints for remote agent pods, effectively reducing the schedulable pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes.

[Less likely] A misconfiguration in the pod's node affinity/selector rules is overly restrictive, preventing pods from landing on nodes that could otherwise host them — but this would be a pre-existing condition, not a new regression, and no suspect changes in sourceDiscovery support this.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for ~141–145 seconds, exceeding the eval's timeout, and no required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever produced.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 are eligible by node affinity/selector for remote agent pods, and both of those nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. Preemption was also ruled out (no preemption victims found). Because the pod could not be scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885) never returned a VM identity or state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion localized to the remote-agent scheduling tier; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-26T20:13–20:18Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes have Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or invoking the runtime, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector for remote agent pods. With no preemption victims available and 4 remaining nodes not matching the pod's affinity rules, every new remote agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state. The eval probe times out waiting for the pod to become ready (~141–151 s), never creates the agent, and returns empty evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the cluster has consumed all allocatable peer-pod VM slots on the only nodes eligible for remote agent pods, leaving no capacity for new pods and no preemption victims to displace.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, artificially constraining scheduling to only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or a node label was removed, effective capacity is reduced even if raw VM slots exist on other nodes.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or real workloads are competing for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, transient exhaustion could cause scheduling failures that resolve once workloads complete.
Quaternary — a stuck or leaked remote agent pod from a prior eval run consuming a VM slot without releasing it, reducing available capacity below the threshold needed for new pods.
